## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| main | src/main.ts |

This script serves as the primary entry point for the application, responsible for bootstrapping the Angular application instance. Its core responsibility is to initialize the application environment and ensure necessary global functionalities are available before the application starts rendering. It also includes a utility extension to enhance the native JavaScript `String` prototype.

Architecturally, this file acts as the application's bootstrap controller. It initializes the main `App` component using the configuration defined in `app/app.config`. Furthermore, it integrates the external `omega-game-engine` library into the global `window` scope, making it accessible throughout the application context.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| String.prototype.capitalize | Method | Capitalizes the first letter of the string instance it is called upon. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The script first checks if `String.prototype.capitalize` exists; if not, it defines this method to convert the first character to uppercase while preserving the rest of the string. It then initializes the Angular application using `bootstrapApplication` and registers the `omega-game-engine` globally.

- **Side Effects:** Mutates the global `String.prototype` object and modifies the global `window` object by assigning the `omega-game-engine` instance.

- **Error Handling:** It uses `.catch((err) => console.error(err))` on the `bootstrapApplication` call to catch and log any errors that occur during the application bootstrapping process.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `@angular/platform-browser`, `omega-game-engine`
- **Internal:** [app/app.config](/src/app/app.config.md), [app/app](/src/app/app.md)

It handles asynchronous dependency loading, initializes the editor instance with custom theming, and manages specialized features like custom GLSL language support and context-aware IntelliSense completions. Its core role is abstracting the complex Monaco API, providing clean methods for model manipulation, marker tracking, and resource disposal.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| MonacoService | code-editor/monaco.service |

This component is responsible for encapsulating the entire lifecycle and interaction with the Monaco Editor instance within an Angular application context. Its primary responsibility is to initialize, configure, and manage the editor, providing specialized features such as custom language support for GLSL shaders and advanced IntelliSense completions for mathematical functions.

It functions as a dedicated service layer, abstracting the complexity of the Monaco Editor API from the rest of the application. It integrates deeply with the UI by handling theme application, event subscriptions (like saving and marker changes), and managing the loading of external dependencies, fitting squarely into the application's core service architecture.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `loadDependencies(onReady: () => void)` | Method | Loads the Monaco Editor dependencies asynchronously by injecting a script tag and waiting for the `require` function to be available. |
| `createEditor(container: HTMLElement, onSave: () => void, onMarkerChange: (errors: number, warnings: number) => void): any` | Method | Initializes and returns a configured Monaco Editor instance bound to a specified DOM container, setting up event listeners for saving and error/warning tracking. |
| `setModel(model: any)` | Method | Sets the content model of the existing editor instance to a provided model. |
| `getModelValue(): string` | Method | Retrieves the current text content from the editor model. |
| `clearAllModelMarkers(source: string)` | Method | Removes all diagnostic markers (errors/warnings) from the editor model associated with a given source. |
| `setModelMarkers(source: string, errorMarkers: any[])` | Method | Applies a set of diagnostic markers (errors/warnings) to the editor model. |
| `createOrGetModel(path: string, content: string, language: string): any` | Method | Creates a new Monaco model or retrieves an existing one based on the provided file path and content, automatically determining the correct language ID. |
| `updateIntelliSenseDefinitions(filePath: string, declarationContent: string): void` | Method | Adds an external library definition to the TypeScript language service, allowing the editor to understand custom types defined in the provided content. |
| `isEditorReady(): boolean` | Method | Checks if the Monaco Editor instance has been successfully initialized. |
| `disposeEditor(): void` | Method | Cleans up all resources associated with the editor, including disposing of extra library definitions and destroying the editor instance. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service manages two primary feature sets: a custom GLSL language provider using Monarch tokens for syntax highlighting, and a completion provider that offers context-aware suggestions. It uses a static map (`NATIVE_GLSL_BUILTINS`) to provide rich, snippet-enabled suggestions for mathematical functions when the user is typing in GLSL mode. It also dynamically loads the Monaco library via a script tag if it's not already present on the window object.
- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with the global `window` object to load external scripts (`loader.js`) and utilizes `document.body.appendChild` for dependency loading. It mutates the state of the editor instance (`this.editorInstance`) and manages external library handles via `this.extraLibs`.
- **Error Handling:** The `loadDependencies` method uses `onload` callbacks to handle the asynchronous loading of the Monaco library. The `createEditor` method relies on the existence of the `monaco` object on `window` before proceeding with configuration.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `@angular/core`
- **Internal:** None

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| AssetCodeService | code-editor/asset-code.service |

This service is responsible for managing all interactions between the frontend application and the backend API endpoints related to project code assets. Its primary responsibility is to abstract the HTTP communication layer, providing typed methods for retrieving, creating, updating, and deleting files within a specified project structure.

This component functions as a dedicated service layer within the application architecture. It utilizes the `HttpClient` to communicate with the API, relying on configuration from `src/app/api/api-url.token` to determine the correct base URL for project-specific code operations. It acts as the intermediary between the application logic and the remote code management system.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| getWorkspaceTree | Method | Fetches the hierarchical structure of files and directories for a given project ID. |
| getFileContent | Method | Retrieves the content of a specific file identified by its path within a project. |
| createFile | Method | Sends a request to create a new file in the project, accepting a `CreateFileRequest` payload. |
| updateFileContent | Method | Sends a request to modify the content of an existing file, accepting an `UpdateFileContentRequest` payload. |
| deleteFile | Method | Deletes a file from the project using its path. |
| getEngineTypings | Method | Fetches the engine-specific type definitions as a raw string. |
| getWorkspaceTypings | Method | Fetches the workspace-specific type definitions as a raw string. |
| compileWorkspace | Method | Triggers a compilation process for the entire workspace and returns the compilation result. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service constructs specific RESTful API endpoints based on the provided `projectId` and the base URL derived from `API_URL`. It maps high-level operations (like `createFile` or `deleteFile`) to the appropriate HTTP methods (POST, DELETE) and endpoint paths.
- **Side Effects:** The code heavily interacts with the network via `HttpClient` to perform GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE requests to the backend API.
- **Error Handling:** Standard RxJS observable patterns are used; specific error handling (like catching HTTP errors) is delegated to the calling components, as the service returns Observables.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
- `API_URL`  Defines the base URL for the backend API. If it ends with `/api`, the service appends `/projects`; otherwise, it prepends `/api/projects`.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `HttpClient`, `Observable`
- **Internal:** [asset-code.models](/code-editor/asset-code.models.md)

nodes.name: EngineLogger
nodes.semantic_summary: EngineLogger implements a Singleton pattern to provide a centralized, thread-safe logging mechanism for the application. It manages log entries internally, enforcing a maximum buffer size by discarding the oldest entries when the limit is reached. It exposes static methods for logging at debug, info, and error levels, while also providing access to the stored log history.
nodes.human_overview:
This component provides a centralized, singleton logging mechanism for the application. Its primary responsibility is to capture, format, and store various levels of operational messagessuch as debug, info, and errorensuring that logs are consistently recorded throughout the system's lifecycle. It manages an internal buffer to prevent unbounded memory growth by automatically discarding the oldest entries when the maximum log limit is reached.

EngineLogger functions as a core utility service within the application architecture. By implementing the Singleton pattern, it guarantees a single point of truth for logging operations across all modules. It interfaces directly with the console for immediate output while persisting structured data internally, allowing other components to retrieve historical logs via the [getLogs](/engine/logger.md) method.
nodes.side_effects: Mutates internal state (the `logs` array) and interacts with the standard console output (`console.log`, `console.debug`, `console.error`).

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| EngineLogger | engine/logger.md |

This component provides a centralized, singleton logging mechanism for the application. Its primary responsibility is to capture, format, and store various levels of operational messagessuch as debug, info, and errorensuring that logs are consistently recorded throughout the system's lifecycle. It manages an internal buffer to prevent unbounded memory growth by automatically discarding the oldest entries when the maximum log limit is reached.

EngineLogger functions as a core utility service within the application architecture. By implementing the Singleton pattern, it guarantees a single point of truth for logging operations across all modules. It interfaces directly with the console for immediate output while persisting structured data internally, allowing other components to retrieve historical logs via the [getLogs](/engine/logger.md) method.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| log | Static Method | Logs a general message. Accepts optional parameters which can be serialized or processed as errors/stacks. |
| debug | Static Method | Logs a debug-level message. Accepts optional parameters which can be serialized or processed as errors/stacks. |
| error | Static Method | Logs an error-level message. Accepts optional parameters which can be serialized or processed as errors/stacks. |
| getLogs | Static Method | Returns the current array of stored log entries. |
| clear | Static Method | Resets the internal log buffer to an empty state. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The logger uses a private static instance to enforce the Singleton pattern. When logging, it processes optional parameters: if an argument is an `Error`, it extracts the message and sanitizes the stack trace; if it's a string containing "at ", it sanitizes it as a stack trace; otherwise, it stringifies objects or converts primitives to strings. All processed entries are pushed to the internal `logs` array, which is capped at `maxLogs` by shifting the oldest entry if the limit is exceeded.

- **Side Effects:** Mutates internal state (the `logs` array) and interacts with the standard console output (`console.log`, `console.debug`, `console.error`).

- **Error Handling:** Errors passed as parameters are captured, and their stack traces are sanitized using `sanitizeStack` before being stored.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** None
- **Internal:** None

nodes.name: authGuard
nodes.semantic_summary: This component implements an Angular CanActivateFn guard responsible for enforcing route-level authentication. It injects AuthService to check the user's login status via isLoggedIn(). If the user is authenticated, navigation proceeds; otherwise, it programmatically redirects the user to the '/login' route using the Router service. It acts as a critical gatekeeper for protected application routes.
nodes.human_overview:
This guard is responsible for enforcing authentication checks on specific routes within the application. Its primary function is to determine, before a route is activated, whether the currently logged-in user possesses the necessary credentials to view the requested page. If the user is not authenticated, the guard prevents navigation to the protected route.

Architecturally, this component acts as a routing middleware or gatekeeper. It leverages the `AuthService` to query the current authentication state and utilizes the `Router` service to programmatically redirect the user to the `/login` page if the authentication check fails.
nodes.side_effects: Interacts with the application state by calling methods on `AuthService` and triggers navigation via the `Router` service.

| Editor | /editor/editor.md |

This component serves as the primary container and orchestrator for the entire editor application interface. Its main responsibility is to manage the lifecycle of the editing environment, including initializing the game engine, loading scenes from assets or storage, and coordinating the various UI panels and behaviors required for interactive scene manipulation.

Architecturally, the `Editor` component acts as a high-level controller, integrating numerous specialized services and sub-components. It relies heavily on [EditorService](/editor/editor.md) for core engine operations, [EditorSettingsService](/editor/editor.md) for configuration management, and manages the state flow between the [SceneTree](/editor/scene-tree/scene-tree.md), [Canvas](/editor/components/canvas/canvas.md), and various behavioral systems like [GizmosBoxBehaviour](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/gizmos-behaviour.md).

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
This file contains no public exports.

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component initializes by subscribing to various state change events from services like [SceneTreeService](/editor/services/scene-tree.service.md) and [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md). Scene loading is triggered via route parameters, fetching serialized data from [AssetService](/editor/api/services/asset.service.md). Once loaded, it initializes editor behaviors (Grid, Gizmos, Picker) and manages the rendering loop via event subscriptions. State persistence is handled by saving the scene object to `sessionStorage` on Ctrl+S.

- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with the network via [AssetService](/editor/api/services/asset.service.md) for loading and saving scene assets. It reads and writes to `sessionStorage` for local scene persistence. It mutates the global state via `(window as any)["omegaEditor"] = this;` and interacts with the underlying WebGL context.

- **Error Handling:** Catches errors during scene JSON parsing and asset loading, logging them via [EngineLogger](/src/engine/logger.md) and hiding the loading indicator. It also handles navigation to an invalid project route if parameters are missing during initialization.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `rxjs`, `angular/core`, `angular/router`.
- **Internal:** [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md), [SceneTreeService](/editor/services/scene-tree.service.md), [EditorSettingsService](/editor/services/editor.settings.md), [EditorStateService](/editor/services/editor-state.service.md), [WindowService](/editor/services/window.service.md), [AssetService](/editor/api/services/asset.service.md), [LoadingService](/src/app/services/loading.service.md), [EditorGridBehaviour](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/grid-behaviour.md), [GizmosBoxBehaviour](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/gizmos-behaviour.md), [EditorEntityPicker](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/entitypick.behaviour.md), [Scene](/omega-game-engine/scene.md), [SceneEntity](/omega-game-engine/scene-entity.md), [JsonSerializedData](/omega-game-engine/json-serialized-data.md), [SceneManager](/omega-game-engine/scene-manager.md), [Colors](/omega-game-engine/colors.md), [Engine](/omega-game-engine/engine.md), [EngineStats](/editor/components/canvas/canvas.md), [EditorSettings](/editor/interfaces/editor-settings.md).

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| App | app/app.md |

This component serves as the root application container, responsible for initializing and managing the entire rendering and simulation environment within the application. Its primary responsibility is to orchestrate the lifecycle of the 3D scene, handling the setup of the WebGL context, loading necessary assets, and establishing the core physics and rendering systems required for the editor.

Architecturally, `App` acts as the main controller for the editor view. It subscribes to events from [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md) to trigger scene loading and context creation. It manages the state of the primary [Scene](/omega-game-engine/scene.md) and integrates various subsystems like the [AudioEngine](/omega-game-engine/audio-engine.md) and camera controls, providing the central hub for the editor's functionality.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
This file contains no public exports.

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component initializes by subscribing to events from [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md). Upon receiving the rendering context, it checks for a "write-scene" query parameter to asynchronously create a new scene. Scene initialization involves loading assets (lights, primitives, textures), setting up the camera, and configuring the audio engine diagnostics suite. Entity creation is handled via `createEntity`, which abstracts the process of attaching rendering behaviors and materials to scene entities.

- **Side Effects:** The code interacts heavily with external state and resources. It initializes and mutates the global `Scene` object, reads parameters from the `ActivatedRoute`, and utilizes the `LoadingService` to manage UI state. It also performs asynchronous asset loading via `EngineCache`.

- **Error Handling:** The component relies on the underlying services and engine to handle most operational errors. Fallback mechanisms are present in `createEntity` where a default `LitMaterial` is used if no specific shader or material is provided.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| CodeWorkspaceComponent | [code-editor/editor/code-editor.component](/code-editor/editor/code-editor.component.md) |

This component is the primary view responsible for managing the entire code editing environment, including the display of files, the active editor instance, and the overall workspace state. Its core responsibility is to orchestrate the loading, display, and persistence of project files, handling user interactions such as opening, closing, and modifying tabs within the editor interface.

Architecturally, `CodeWorkspaceComponent` acts as a high-level controller for the editor view. It integrates services like [AssetCodeService](/asset-code/asset-code.service.md) to fetch file content and workspace structure, [MonacoService](/monaco/monaco.service.md) to manage the editor instances, and [EditorStateService](/editor/services/editor-state.service.md) to react to global project changes. It manages the UI state for tabs, saving, and compilation status.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| EditorTab | Interface | Defines the structure for a single tab, including file metadata, dirty status, and the associated Monaco model. |
| ToastMessage | Interface | Defines the structure for transient notification messages displayed to the user. |
| CodeWorkspaceComponent | Class | Manages the lifecycle and state of the code editing workspace. |
| onGlobalContextMenu | Method | Handles the global context menu event, preventing default browser behavior. |
| closeContextMenu | Method | Hides the context menu when the user clicks anywhere on the document. |
| unloadNotification | Method | Intercepts the browser's beforeunload event to prompt the user about unsaved changes. |
| loadIntelliSenseDefinitions | Method | Fetches and applies type definitions for both the engine and user project scopes to the Monaco editor. |
| loadWorkspaceTree | Method | Fetches the directory structure of the current project and populates the workspace tree. |
| handleNodeClick | Method | Handles clicks on nodes in the workspace tree, either selecting an existing tab or loading a new file. |
| createNewTab | Method | Instantiates a new `EditorTab` and initializes the corresponding Monaco model for a given file result. |
| selectTab | Method | Sets the active tab and ensures the Monaco editor displays the content of that tab. |
| closeTab | Method | Initiates the process of closing a specific tab, prompting for confirmation if changes are unsaved. |
| forceCloseTab | Method | Programmatically closes a tab, disposing of its associated model and listener. |
| closeAllTabsWithoutCheck | Method | Clears all open tabs and disposes of all associated editor resources. |
| hasUnsavedChanges | Method | Checks if any open tabs have been modified since the last save. |
| triggerGoBack | Method | Navigates the user back to the main canvas view, prompting if unsaved changes exist. |
| openContextMenu | Method | Displays the context menu at the specified coordinates for a given workspace node. |
| triggerCreateFileAtRoot | Method | Prompts the user to create a new file directly at the root of the current project. |
| triggerCreateFileInFolder | Method | Prompts the user to create a new file within a selected folder node. |
| triggerDeleteNode | Method | Deletes a specified file or folder node from the workspace, after user confirmation. |
| triggerDeleteNodeFromMenu | Method | Triggers the deletion of the currently selected context menu node. |
| saveCurrentChanges | Method | Persists the content of the active editor tab to the backend service, triggering a compilation check upon success. |
| executeWorkspaceCompilation | Method | Triggers a full workspace compilation process, updating the UI with success/error markers. |
| calculatePadding | Method | Calculates an estimated padding value based on the depth of a file path. |
| findFirstFile | Method | Recursively searches a directory node to find the first file within it. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component operates around a reactive lifecycle driven by `effect` tied to `EditorStateService.activeProject()`. When a project is active, it loads the workspace tree and initializes Monaco. File content changes trigger a dirty flag update, which, upon saving, initiates a full workspace compilation via `AssetCodeService`. The compilation step uses Monaco's marker system to visually represent compiler errors and warnings.
- **Side Effects:** The component heavily interacts with external systems: it makes numerous network calls via `AssetCodeService` (e.g., `getWorkspaceTree`, `getFileContent`, `updateFileContent`, `compileWorkspace`). It also interacts with the browser environment via `HostListener` events (`contextmenu`, `beforeunload`) and uses `prompt()` for user input.
- **Error Handling:** Network failures during file loading or saving result in `showToast` notifications and the hiding of the loading backdrop. Compilation errors are caught, and specific error markers are applied to the Monaco editor using `monacoService.setModelMarkers`.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `rxjs`, `@angular/core`
- **Internal:** [AssetCodeService](/asset-code/asset-code.service.md), [EditorStateService](/editor/services/editor-state.service.md), [LoadingService](/app/services/loading.service.md), [MonacoService](/monaco/monaco.service.md), [Router](/angular/router.md)

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| dotnet-legacy | /assets/wasm/dotnet-legacy.d.md |

This component provides a set of TypeScript declarations for legacy interoperability bindings between JavaScript/TypeScript and a .NET runtime compiled to WebAssembly (Wasm). Its primary responsibility is to define the interfaces and types necessary to interact with low-level memory management, object references, and runtime functions exposed by the Wasm environment.

This file serves as a foundational layer within the application's architecture, specifically acting as a bridge or adapter layer. It exposes deprecated APIs (`BINDINGType` and `MONOType`) that allow older code paths to interact with the core runtime, while also defining the fundamental data structures like `MonoObject` and `WasmRoot` that underpin the managed environment.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ManagedPointer | Interface | Represents a managed pointer type within the Wasm environment. |
| NativePointer | Interface | Represents a native pointer type within the Wasm environment. |
| VoidPtr | Interface | An extension of `NativePointer` used to denote a void pointer. |
| MonoObject | Interface | The base interface for managed objects in the runtime. |
| MonoString | Interface | Represents a managed string object. |
| MonoArray | Interface | Represents a managed array object. |
| MonoObjectRef | Interface | Represents a reference to a managed object. |
| WasmRoot | Interface | Defines the interface for a managed root object, providing methods for access, manipulation, and lifecycle management. |
| WasmRootBuffer | Interface | Defines the interface for a managed buffer root, allowing indexed access to managed pointers. |
| BINDINGType | Type | A collection of deprecated functions for static binding and runtime entry point calls. |
| MONOType | Type | A collection of deprecated functions for runtime configuration, memory manipulation, and object creation. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** This file is purely a set of type definitions (`declare interface`, `type`). It does not contain executable logic, algorithms, or state flow. It defines the contract for how external JavaScript code should interact with the underlying Wasm runtime functions.

- **Side Effects:** None. It is a declaration file and has no runtime side effects.

- **Error Handling:** None. As a declaration file, it defines potential behaviors but does not implement error handling.

**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

This file serves as a TypeScript declaration file (`.d.ts`) defining the public interface for the .NET runtime environment when compiled to WebAssembly (Wasm). Its primary responsibility is to provide type safety and structure for JavaScript code interacting with the low-level Wasm runtime, exposing APIs for memory management, I/O, and application bootstrapping.

It acts as a critical bridge between the JavaScript host environment and the compiled .NET runtime instance. It defines complex types like `EmscriptenModule`, `DotnetHostBuilder`, and `RuntimeAPI`, allowing developers to configure, initialize, and execute .NET applications within a browser context without needing to know the underlying C# implementation details.
nodes.side_effects: The types define interactions with external systems: `DotnetHostBuilder` methods like `create()` and `run()` inherently involve network I/O (fetching resources) and global state mutation (setting up the runtime). The `EmscriptenModule` methods like `_malloc` and `_free` directly interact with the underlying Wasm memory heap.
nodes.raw_markdown:
## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| dotnet.d | /assets/wasm/dotnet.d.md |

This file serves as a TypeScript declaration file (`.d.ts`) defining the public interface for the .NET runtime environment when compiled to WebAssembly (Wasm). Its primary responsibility is to provide type safety and structure for JavaScript code interacting with the low-level Wasm runtime, exposing APIs for memory management, I/O, and application bootstrapping.

It acts as a critical bridge between the JavaScript host environment and the compiled .NET runtime instance. It defines complex types like `EmscriptenModule`, `DotnetHostBuilder`, and `RuntimeAPI`, allowing developers to configure, initialize, and execute .NET applications within a browser context without needing to know the underlying C# implementation details.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NativePointer` | Interface | Represents a raw memory pointer within the Wasm heap. |
| `VoidPtr` | Interface | A pointer type specifically designated as void. |
| `CharPtr` | Interface | A pointer type specifically designated as a character pointer. |
| `Int32Ptr` | Interface | A pointer type specifically designated as a 32-bit integer pointer. |
| `EmscriptenModule` | Interface | Defines core Wasm runtime functions like memory access (`HEAP8`, `_malloc`), calling native functions (`ccall`, `cwrap`), and I/O utilities. |
| `DotnetHostBuilder` | Interface | Provides a fluent builder pattern for configuring the .NET runtime startup process, allowing settings for resources, environment variables, and application arguments. |
| `MonoConfig` | Type | Configuration object used by `DotnetHostBuilder` to specify runtime settings such as resource locations, debugging levels, and globalization modes. |
| `ResourceGroups` | Interface | Defines how various types of assets (assembly, PDB, Wasm symbols, etc.) should be loaded and managed during runtime initialization. |
| `ResourceList` | Type | A map defining specific asset names and their optional integrity hashes. |
| `LoadBootResourceCallback` | Type | A callback function used by `DotnetHostBuilder` to override the default mechanism for fetching boot resources from custom sources like CDNs. |
| `LoadingResource` | Interface | Describes a resource being loaded, including its name, URL, and the promise representing its download. |
| `AssetEntry` | Interface | A detailed structure describing a single asset, including its behavior, resolved URL, and optional buffer data. |
| `SingleAssetBehaviors` | Type | Enumeration defining the specific role an asset plays (e.g., "dotnetwasm", "resource", "assembly"). |
| `AssetBehaviors` | Type | A union type encompassing all possible behaviors for loading assets. |
| `GlobalizationMode` | Enum | Defines how the runtime should handle internationalization data (e.g., "Sharded", "All", "Invariant"). |
| `DotnetModuleConfig` | Type | Configuration object passed to `createDotnetRuntime` to customize the module loading process. |
| `APIType` | Type | Defines the set of high-level API methods available after the runtime is initialized, including running the main application and accessing heap memory. |
| `RuntimeAPI` | Type | The final object returned upon successful runtime initialization, containing the `Module` interface and the high-level `APIType`. |
| `ModuleAPI` | Type | A wrapper interface providing access to the `dotnet` builder and an `exit` function. |
| `IDisposable` | Interface | Defines a contract for objects that can be explicitly cleaned up via a `dispose()` method. |
| `IMemoryView` | Interface | Extends `IDisposable` and provides methods for reading and writing data between the Wasm memory and JavaScript typed arrays. |
| `mono_exit` | Function | The external function declared to signal the runtime to exit with a specific code. |
| `dotnet` | Constant | The globally available instance of `DotnetHostBuilder` for immediate configuration. |
| `exit` | Constant | The globally available function wrapper for `mono_exit`. |
| `getDotnetRuntime` | Function | A global function used to retrieve an initialized `RuntimeAPI` instance based on a runtime ID. |
| `createDotnetRuntime` | Function | The primary factory function used to initialize and return a `RuntimeAPI` instance based on provided configuration. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component primarily defines interfaces and types rather than implementing logic. The core functionality is encapsulated within the `DotnetHostBuilder` and `createDotnetRuntime` functions, which manage the complex asynchronous process of loading, configuring, and instantiating the Wasm runtime environment.
- **Side Effects:** The types define interactions with external systems: `DotnetHostBuilder` methods like `create()` and `run()` inherently involve network I/O (fetching resources) and global state mutation (setting up the runtime). The `EmscriptenModule` methods like `_malloc` and `_free` directly interact with the underlying Wasm memory heap.
- **Error Handling:** The `DotnetHostBuilder` supports configuration options like `ignorePdbLoadErrors` to manage failure modes during resource loading. The `onAbort` and `onExit` callbacks within `EmscriptenModule` provide mechanisms for handling runtime termination or errors.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** None.
- **Internal:** None.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| PhysicsEngineBridge | /engine/phisics/bridge.md |

This abstract class defines the contract for bridging the application's internal simulation logic with an external physics engine implementation. Its primary responsibility is to abstract away the specific details of the underlying physics library, providing a standardized interface for managing entities, applying forces, and querying physical states within the game world.

This component acts as a crucial service layer within the application architecture. It sits between the core game logic and the specialized physics simulation, allowing the rest of the system to interact with physics concepts (like gravity or raycasting) without needing to know if the backend is using Box2D, PhysX, or a custom implementation.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PhysicsEngineBridge | Class | Abstract base class defining the required interface for any physics engine implementation. |
| initialize | Method | Sets up the physics world using the provided settings. |
| step | Method | Advances the physics simulation by a given time delta. |
| destroy | Method | Cleans up all resources associated with the physics engine. |
| registerEntity | Method | Adds a new entity to the physics simulation, associating it with its components. |
| unregisterEntity | Method | Removes an entity from the physics simulation. |
| syncToPhysics | Method | Pushes the current transform of an entity from the application state into the physics simulation. |
| getTransformFromPhysics | Method | Retrieves the calculated physical transform of an entity from the simulation. |
| setGravity | Method | Modifies the global gravitational force applied across the physics world. |
| raycast | Method | Performs a ray intersection test against colliders in the physics world. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The class itself contains no core logic; it is a pure interface definition. Concrete implementations must manage the lifecycle of the external physics engine, handling initialization, iterative stepping, and state synchronization between the application's data structures and the engine's internal state.

- **Side Effects:** Concrete implementations will inherently interact with external state (the physics engine instance) and potentially mutate global state (e.g., setting gravity).

- **Error Handling:** The `initialize` method returns a `Promise<void>`, indicating that initialization might involve asynchronous setup and could reject upon failure.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

| PhysicsWorld | engine/phisics/world.md |

This component serves as the primary interface and orchestrator for the entire physics simulation within the application. Its core responsibility is to manage the lifecycle of the physics world, abstracting the complex, low-level interactions with the actual physics engine backend. It handles the registration, updating, and deregistration of physical entities, ensuring they are correctly synchronized between the application's state and the simulation's state.

Architecturally, `PhysicsWorld` acts as a high-level service layer or controller. It sits between the application's core logic (which holds entity data) and the concrete physics implementation provided by `PhysicsEngineBridge`. It relies on `PhysicsWorldSettings` for configuration and interacts with components like `RigidbodyComponent` and `ColliderComponent` to define the physical properties of entities.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PhysicsWorld | Class | Manages the physics simulation lifecycle, including initialization, entity registration, and simulation stepping. |
| initialize | Method | Sets up the active engine backend bridge using provided settings. |
| registerEntity | Method | Registers or updates an entity within the physics simulation space, providing its physical components. |
| unregisterEntity | Method | Removes an entity completely from the physics simulation loop. |
| update | Method | The main ticker function that steps the simulation forward, synchronizing data both to and from the physics engine. |
| setGravity | Method | Applies global gravity settings to the active physics backend. |
| destroy | Method | Cleans up all resources associated with the physics world and the backend bridge. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The `update` method implements a three-stage synchronization loop: first, it pushes any externally modified entity transforms to the physics engine (`syncToPhysics`); second, it advances the simulation time step (`step(dt)`); and third, it pulls the resulting transforms from the physics engine back into the application state (`getTransformFromPhysics`). Entity management relies on an internal `Set` (`registeredEntities`) to track active simulation participants.

- **Side Effects:** Mutates external state by calling methods on the injected `PhysicsEngineBridge` instance, which represents the external physics engine. It also logs initialization status to the console.

- **Error Handling:** The component uses null checks (`if (!this.activeBridge) return;`) extensively to prevent runtime errors if initialization has not occurred or if the world has been destroyed.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** None
- **Internal:** [PhysicsEngineBridge](/engine/phisics/bridge.md), [PhysicsWorldSettings](/engine/phisics/components.md), [RigidbodyComponent](/engine/phisics/components.md), [ColliderComponent](/engine/phisics/components.md)

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `makeDynamic` | Method | Configures the rigidbody to be dynamic, setting a specified mass. |

| `setLinearVelocity` | Method | Directly sets the linear velocity of the entity's underlying physics body. |

- **Core Logic:** The class initializes with a `PhysicsWorld` instance. Configuration methods (`makeDynamic`, `makeStatic`, `addBoxCollider`) modify the internal state of the `RigidbodyComponent` and `ColliderComponent`. Runtime methods (`applyForce`, `setLinearVelocity`) access the internal reference (`internalBodyRef`) of the rigidbody to directly manipulate the underlying physics engine body's state.
- **Side Effects:** Mutates the state of the internal `RigidbodyComponent` and `ColliderComponent`. The `enableSimulation` method is designed to interact with the external `PhysicsWorld` to register the entity, which constitutes a side effect on the global simulation state.
- **Error Handling:** The `applyForce` and `setLinearVelocity` methods include checks (`if (rawBody)`) to prevent runtime errors if the underlying physics body reference (`internalBodyRef`) has not been initialized or is null.

This component serves as a dedicated bridge layer, abstracting the complex physics simulation provided by the Rapier 3D library into the engine's internal component model. Its primary responsibility is to manage the lifecycle of physical entitiescreating, updating, and destroying rigid bodies and colliders within the Rapier world based on the engine's `RigidbodyComponent` and `ColliderComponent` data.

Architecturally, `RapierPhysicsBridge` acts as a specialized service layer within the physics subsystem. It interfaces between the high-level entity management system and the low-level physics simulation engine. It relies on `PhysicsWorldSettings` for initialization parameters and exposes methods to synchronize entity transforms and perform physics queries like raycasting, allowing other parts of the application to interact with the simulation state.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `RapierPhysicsBridge` | Class | Manages the Rapier physics world, handling entity registration, simulation stepping, and data synchronization. |
| `initialize(settings: PhysicsWorldSettings): Promise<void>` | Method | Initializes the Rapier world, including loading the WebAssembly binary and setting up gravity based on provided settings. |
| `registerEntity(entityId: string, rb: RigidbodyComponent, col?: ColliderComponent, transform?: PhysicsTransform): void` | Method | Creates a rigid body and associated collider in the Rapier world for a given entity, mapping engine components to Rapier structures. |
| `unregisterEntity(entityId: string): void` | Method | Removes a registered rigid body and collider from the Rapier world using the entity ID. |
| `syncToPhysics(entityId: string, transform: PhysicsTransform): void` | Method | Forces the Rapier body's position and rotation to match the provided engine transform, useful for editor synchronization. |
| `getTransformFromPhysics(entityId: string): PhysicsTransform | null` | Method | Retrieves the current position and rotation of a registered entity directly from the Rapier simulation. |
| `step(dt: number): void` | Method | Advances the physics simulation by the given time step (`dt`). |
| `setGravity(x: number, y: number, z: number): void` | Method | Updates the global gravity vector applied to the entire physics world. |
| `raycast(origin: Vector3D, direction: Vector3D, maxDistance: number)` | Method | Performs a raycast query against all colliders in the world, returning hit information if an intersection occurs. |
| `dispose(): void` | Method | Cleans up all registered bodies and frees the underlying Rapier WebAssembly resources. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component uses a `Map` (`bodyMap`) to maintain a direct reference between the engine's string entity IDs and the native `RAPIER.RigidBody` handles. Entity registration involves translating engine component types (e.g., `RigidbodyType.Static`) into corresponding Rapier descriptions (`RAPIER.RigidBodyDesc.fixed()`) and creating the body and collider within the `RAPIER.World`. The simulation advances via `world.step()`, which integrates forces and calculates collisions based on the provided time step.
- **Side Effects:** Mutates the internal state of the `RAPIER.World` instance, which represents the external physics simulation environment. It manages the lifecycle of these external simulation objects.
- **Error Handling:** The `raycast` method handles the possibility of no collision by returning `null`. Entity removal relies on checking if the body exists in `bodyMap` before attempting removal.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `@dimforge/rapier3d`
- **Internal:** [components](/components.md)

| `movableHandleId` | Input | The required ID of the child element used as the drag handle. |
| `resizeHandleId` | Input | The optional ID of the child element used as the resize handle. |
| `showResize` | Input | Boolean flag determining if the directive should automatically create a default resize handle. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The directive initializes by locating the specified drag and resize handles. It reads the element's initial CSS `transform` state to establish starting coordinates. Dragging is managed by listening to `mousedown` on the handle, followed by `mousemove` on the document, which uses `requestAnimationFrame` to calculate and apply new `translate` values while clamping movement within viewport boundaries. Resizing follows a similar pattern, calculating new width/height based on mouse movement relative to the start point.
- **Side Effects:** Mutates the global state by modifying the `style` and `cursor` properties of the host element and the `document.body`. It also uses `requestAnimationFrame` to schedule updates.
- **Error Handling:** It logs an error to the console if the required `movableHandleId` cannot be found during initialization.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `@angular/core`
- **Internal:** None

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| DragHandleDirective | editor/directives/mouse-drag.directive |

This directive provides robust, low-level drag-and-drop functionality to any HTML element designated as a "handle." Its primary responsibility is to capture mouse events (`mousedown`, `mousemove`, `mouseup`) on the host element and translate physical mouse movement into structured `DragEventData`. It allows fine-grained control over the dragging behavior via inputs like `dragMode` (horizontal, vertical, or both) and `movementThreshold`.

Architecturally, this directive functions as a specialized UI behavior modifier. It is designed to be applied to a specific handle element, which then emits events that are consumed by a parent component responsible for managing the state and position of a larger, draggable element. It acts as a bridge between raw DOM events and application-level movement logic, fitting within the UI component layer.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| DragMode | Type | Defines the allowed axis for dragging: 'horizontal', 'vertical', or 'both'. |
| DragEventData | Interface | Contains the movement data emitted during a drag operation: `deltaX`, `deltaY`, `distanceX`, and `distanceY`. |
| DragHandleDirective | Class | Implements the drag functionality, listening for mouse events and emitting the `drag` event. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The directive initializes the drag state upon `mousedown`, capturing starting coordinates. It then attaches global listeners to the `document` for `mousemove` and `mouseup`. During `mousemove`, it calculates the change in position, applies restrictions based on `dragMode`, and only emits the `drag` event if the movement exceeds `movementThreshold`. Upon `mouseup`, it cleans up all listeners and resets the state.

- **Side Effects:** Mutates global state by modifying the `document.body` style (setting `cursor` and adding/removing the `no-select` class) during the drag operation. It also manages global event listeners attached to the `document`.

- **Error Handling:** The directive relies on the `OnDestroy` lifecycle hook to ensure that `onMouseUp()` is called, which safely detaches all global event listeners, preventing memory leaks.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `@angular/core`
- **Internal:** None

This service is responsible for managing the state and lifecycle of multiple editor windows within the application. Its primary responsibility is to maintain a collection of active window configurations, track which window is currently focused, and manage the visual stacking order (z-index) of these windows as user interactions occur.

Architecturally, `WindowService` functions as a central state management utility. It holds the canonical list of windows via `windows$` and the currently active window ID via `activeWindowId$`. It interacts with the application state by providing methods like `open`, `focus`, and `close`, which modify the internal state and notify subscribers of changes, fitting the role of a core application service.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| WindowService | Class | Manages the collection, focus, and stacking order of editor windows. |
| windows$ | Observable | Stream emitting the current array of all active `WindowConfig` objects. |
| activeWindowId$ | Observable | Stream emitting the ID of the currently focused window, or `null`. |
| open | Method | Creates a new window instance, assigns it a unique ID and the highest available z-index, and adds it to the active list, automatically focusing it. |
| focus | Method | Sets a specific window as the active window, ensuring it receives the highest possible z-index to bring it to the front. |
| close | Method | Removes a window from the active list. If the closed window was active, it automatically focuses the next highest-stacked window or sets the active ID to `null`. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service maintains two primary state streams: one for the list of all windows and one for the active window ID. When a window is opened, it receives a unique ID and the next sequential z-index. Focusing a window involves iterating over all windows and updating the target window's z-index to the current maximum. Closing a window triggers logic to determine the next active window based on the remaining windows' z-indices.

- **Side Effects:** Mutates internal state managed via RxJS `BehaviorSubject`s, which propagates changes to subscribers.

- **Error Handling:** The `close` method includes logic to handle the edge case where the last window is closed, correctly setting `activeWindowIdSubject` to `null`.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| EditorService | /editor/services/editor.service.md |

This component serves as the central orchestration service for the editor environment, managing the lifecycle of the game engine, scene loading, and editor-specific interactions like camera control and gizmo manipulation. Its primary responsibility is to provide a unified interface through which other parts of the application can interact with the underlying rendering and simulation capabilities of the game engine.

As a core service, `EditorService` acts as a controller layer, mediating between the application state (managed by [EditorStateService](/editor/services/editor-state.service.md)) and the complex, low-level rendering engine. It exposes numerous event emitters and subjects to allow decoupled components to subscribe to state changes, such as scene loading events or rendering frame updates.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| onSceneLoaded | EventEmitter | Emitted when a scene has been successfully loaded into the engine. |
| onScenePlay | EventEmitter | Emitted when the scene playback is requested. |
| onScenePause | EventEmitter | Emitted when the scene playback is paused. |
| onSceneStop | EventEmitter | Emitted when the scene playback is stopped. |
| onSceneUpdated | EventEmitter | Emitted when the scene state has been updated. |
| onEditorSaveStateRequest | EventEmitter | Emitted to signal a request to save the current editor state. |
| editorRunningState | EventEmitter | Emitted to broadcast the current running state of the editor. |
| onRenderingContextCreated | EventEmitter | Emitted when the WebGL2RenderingContext is available for rendering. |
| onCanvasRequestResize | BehaviorSubject | Subject used to request canvas resizing with new width and height. |
| onCanvasRequestReset | EventEmitter | Emitted to request a reset of the canvas viewport. |
| onRenderFrame | BehaviorSubject | Subject that emits the WebGL2RenderingContext during a render frame. |
| onUpdateFrame | BehaviorSubject | Subject that emits the current frame update count. |
| gizmoMode | BehaviorSubject | Subject controlling the active gizmo mode (e.g., Translate, Rotate). |
| transformSpace | BehaviorSubject | Subject controlling the active coordinate space for transformations (e.g., Local, World). |
| setCanvas | Method | Sets the internal reference to the HTMLCanvasElement used by the editor. |
| get scene | Getter | Returns the currently loaded Scene object. |
| get camera | Getter | Returns the active Camera instance. |
| get gl | Getter | Returns the initialized WebGL2RenderingContext. |
| get gameEngine | Getter | Returns the active Engine instance, initializing it if necessary. |
| setGizmoMode | Method | Updates the active gizmo mode via the `gizmoMode` subject. |
| setTransformSpace | Method | Updates the active transformation space via the `transformSpace` subject. |
| setToggleWorkspacePanel | Method | Controls the visibility of specific workspace panels. |
| reloadEngineRuntime | Method | Asynchronously destroys and reloads the entire game engine runtime based on the active project configuration. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service initializes a default camera upon construction and maintains a reference to the `Engine` instance. Scene loading involves setting the current scene and calling `gameEngine?.loadScene()`. The `reloadEngineRuntime` method handles complex dynamic module loading by constructing a URL pointing to a project's bundled code, fetching it, and instantiating the `Game` class from the loaded module.
- **Side Effects:** The code interacts heavily with external state and systems. It reads authentication tokens from `localStorage` and `sessionStorage`, makes network requests via `apiUrl` to load project bundles, and mutates the internal state of the `Engine` and `Camera` objects.
- **Error Handling:** The `reloadEngineRuntime` method uses a `try...catch` block to handle critical failures during dynamic module loading, logging specific errors related to linker failures or network issues.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
- `API_URL`  The base URL for the application's API endpoints, used to construct dynamic bundle URLs.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `EventEmitter`, `BehaviorSubject` (from RxJS), `Engine`, `Scene`, `Camera`, `CanvasViewport` (from `omega-game-engine`).
- **Internal:** [EditorStateService](/editor/services/editor-state.service.md), [API_URL](/src/app/api/api-url.token.md).

This component is responsible for simulating the celestial mechanics of a day/night cycle within the game engine environment. Its primary responsibility is to dynamically control the position, color, and intensity of the primary directional light (the sun) based on an internal time-of-day clock. It also manages an optional secondary light source (the moon) and updates associated visual elements like skybox colors, cloud movement, and starfield intensity to create a cohesive atmospheric simulation.

As an `EntityBehaviour`, this component acts as a sophisticated controller or service layer attached to a scene entity. It interfaces heavily with the scene's rendering pipeline, specifically interacting with the [SkyboxRenderer](/editor/behaviours/skybox-renderer.md) to drive visual changes, and directly manipulates the properties of the scene's directional lights and scene fog to reflect the current time state.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SunBehaviour | Class | Controls the sun's position, color, and the day/night cycle in the scene. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component uses a time-based system where `timeOfDay` progresses based on `elapsed` time. It calculates the sun's 3D position using trigonometric functions based on the time, simulating an arc path defined by `sunHeight`. It uses `getInterpolationData` to determine the correct color and visual state (e.g., sunrise, noon, night) and then interpolates between defined color palettes (`lighColor`, `dayPhaseColors`) using a `delta` factor. The `_calculateShadowStrength` method manages the transition of shadow intensity between day and night phases.
- **Side Effects:** Mutates external/global state by directly modifying the properties of the scene's directional lights (color, position, active state), the scene's ambient properties (`scene.clearColor`, `scene.sceneFog.color`), and the uniforms of the [SkyboxShader](/editor/behaviours/skybox-shader.md) via the [SkyboxRenderer](/editor/behaviours/skybox-renderer.md).
- **Error Handling:** The `initialize` method checks for the existence of the scene and the `SkyboxRenderer`, falling back to searching the scene objects if the direct parent reference fails. The `update` loop includes checks (`if (!this.parent?.scene) return;`) to prevent runtime errors if the scene context is lost.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

- **Internal:** [omega-game-engine](/omega-game-engine.md)

| onDefaultChanged | Method | Handles changes made to standard properties (string, number, boolean, etc.) within the inspector. |
| onRemoveBehaviourRequested | Method | Initiates the confirmation process to remove the associated behaviour from its parent entity. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component initializes by defining mappings for various rendering enums (`drawingEnums`). When the `behaviour` input is set, `loadProperties` is called, which iterates over these defined enums and boolean flags to construct lists of `ITargetProperty` objects for rendering. It maintains separate lists for enum properties (`_renderProperties`) and boolean properties (`_renderEnable`). Property updates are handled via `onEnumChanged` and `onDefaultChanged`, which directly mutate the `behaviour` object's properties.
- **Side Effects:** Mutates the state of the `EntityBehaviour` object when properties are changed via `onDefaultChanged` or `onEnumChanged`. It also interacts with the external state management via `ConfirmationService` when `onRemoveBehaviourRequested` is called.
- **Error Handling:** The `onRemoveBehaviourRequested` method uses `ConfirmationService` to handle user confirmation before attempting to call `this.behaviour.parent.removeBehaviour(this.behaviour)`, providing a safeguard against accidental removal.

Its primary function is to expose and manage the shader's properties, allowing users to modify shader parameters like fragment and vertex source URIs via dropdown selectors. It abstracts the complexity of shader source management, enabling direct manipulation of the shader instance.

As a specialized extension of [ObjectInspector](/editor/inspectors/object-inspector/object-inspector.md), the `ShaderInspector` acts as a specialized UI controller within the editor's property panel system. It integrates various UI components like [InpectorTogglePanel](/editor/components/inpector-toggle-panel/inpector-toggle-panel.md) and [DropdownComponent](/src/app/components/dropdown/dropdown.md) to present shader-specific controls, ensuring that the shader object's state is correctly synchronized with the editor view.

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ShaderInspector | Class | Extends ObjectInspector to provide specialized property viewing for Shader objects. |

| selectedFrag | Getter | Returns the `DropdownItem` corresponding to the currently selected fragment shader URI. |
| selectedVert | Getter | Returns the `DropdownItem` corresponding to the currently selected vertex shader URI. |
| onDefaultChanged | Method | Handles changes to standard properties on the shader object. |
| onShaderSelected | Method | Updates the shader's URI based on a selection from the shader dropdowns and triggers recompilation. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component initializes by populating dropdown lists (`_shaderFraList` and `_shaderVertList`) by scanning `ShaderSources.frag` and `ShaderSources.vertex` keys, filtering out internal or ignored sources. Changes are applied via `onDefaultChanged` or `onShaderSelected`, which directly mutates the `_shader` instance.
- **Side Effects:** The component mutates the state of the `Shader` object (`this._shader[item.key] = value;`) and explicitly calls `this._shader.recompile()` when a shader URI is selected, which implies an internal engine state change (recompilation).
- **Error Handling:** The `loadProperties` method includes a check (`if (!this._selectedObject?.property)`) to gracefully handle cases where the shader property is not yet available, setting properties to an empty array.

This component is responsible for providing a user interface panel that allows developers to inspect and manipulate the transformation properties (position, rotation, and scale) of a `SceneEntity` within the editor environment. It handles user input, such as dragging handles or modifying input fields, to translate these changes into direct updates on the entity's underlying `Transform` object.

Architecturally, `TransformInspector` functions as a specialized UI component within the editor framework. It consumes a `SceneEntity` via an `@Input()` to gain access to its `Transform`. It relies on services like [ConfirmationService](/src/app/services/confirmation.service.md) for user confirmations and utilizes directives like [DragHandleDirective](/editor/directives/mouse-drag.directive.md) to manage interactive manipulation of the entity's properties.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| entity | Input | The `SceneEntity` whose transform properties are to be inspected and modified. |
| collapsed | Input | A boolean flag determining the visibility state of the inspector panel. |
| onSpanDrag | Method | Handles drag events, applying delta values to translate, rotate, or scale the entity based on the drag side. |
| performAction | Method | Executes the specific transformation action (translate, rotate, or scale) on the `Transform` object based on the provided index. |
| onPositionChanged | Method | Updates the local position of the transform when a position input field changes. |
| onRotationChanged | Method | Updates the local rotation of the transform when a rotation input field changes. |
| onScaleChanged | Method | Updates the local scale of the transform when a scale input field changes. |
| onReset | Method | Prompts the user to confirm a reset action, which sets the entity's local position, rotation, and scale back to identity values. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component manages three primary modes of transformation manipulation: direct input binding (via `onPositionChanged`, `onRotationChanged`, `onScaleChanged`), interactive dragging (via `onSpanDrag`), and a global reset function. When an entity is bound via the `entity` input, the component initializes its internal `Transform` reference and synchronizes its local scale values. All modifications are applied to the `Transform` object, which then calls `updateMatrices()` to reflect the changes in the scene graph.
- **Side Effects:** The code mutates the state of the `Transform` object associated with the bound `SceneEntity`. It also interacts with the `ConfirmationService` to trigger user prompts.
- **Error Handling:** The `onReset` method uses the `ConfirmationService` to guard against accidental state mutation, ensuring that transformation resets only occur upon explicit user confirmation.

This utility class functions as a core mathematical service layer within the scene editor. It relies on camera and viewport data to correctly map screen space to world space, fitting into the geometric calculation pipeline that supports user interaction and object selection within the [Camera](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/camera.md) context.

- **Core Logic:** `screenPointToRay` uses inverse projection and inverse view matrices to transform clip-space coordinates derived from screen coordinates back into world space, yielding the ray direction. `intersectRayWithPlane` uses the standard formula for line-plane intersection, solving for the parameter $t$ where the ray intersects the plane.
- **Side Effects:** None.
- **Error Handling:** `intersectRayWithPlane` handles the case where the ray direction is parallel to the plane by checking if the dot product of the ray direction and plane normal is near zero, returning `null` in that scenario.

This component is responsible for rendering and managing the interactive gizmos (translation, rotation, scaling) that allow users to manipulate `SceneEntity` transformations within the editor viewport. It handles the complex logic of translating mouse input into geometric transformations, utilizing raycasting and picking textures to determine which gizmo handle the user is interacting with.

Architecturally, `GizmosBoxBehaviour` acts as a specialized `RendererBehaviour` within the scene editor context. It subscribes to state changes from [EditorService](/services/editor.service.md) to dynamically adjust its behavior based on the active [GizmoMode](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/gizmo-mode.enum.md) and [TransformSpace](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/transform-space.enum.md). It relies heavily on helper components like [ConeHelper](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/cone.helper.md) and [ScaleBoxHelper](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/scale-box.helper.md) for visual representation.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GizmosBoxBehaviour` | Class | Manages the rendering and interaction logic for scene entity gizmos. |
| `mouseClaimed` | Boolean | Indicates if the gizmo interaction system currently has control over mouse input. |
| `hoveredBoundingBoxColor` | Color | Color used to highlight the bounding box of the currently hovered entity. |
| `hoveredBoundingBoxLineWidth` | Number | Line width used for the bounding box of the currently hovered entity. |
| `hoveredBoundingBox` | BoundingBox | The bounding box of the currently hovered entity. |
| `hoveredEntity` | SceneEntity | The entity currently under the mouse hover. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component operates in two main phases: rendering and interaction. Rendering involves drawing the selected entity's bounding box and the active gizmo based on the current `GizmoMode` (Translate, Scale, Rotate). Interaction is driven by mouse movement and clicks. When the mouse moves, a picking pass is executed using a dedicated shader and texture to identify the clicked handle ID. If a handle is active, the component calculates the necessary transformation (translation, scaling, or rotation) by intersecting the camera ray with a plane defined by the gizmo handle's orientation, updating the entity's transform accordingly.
- **Side Effects:** Mutates external state by directly modifying the `Transform` component of the `SceneEntity` when dragging occurs. It also interacts with the rendering context (`_gl`) to perform drawing operations and read pixel data from the picking texture.
- **Error Handling:** Fallbacks are implemented when `selectedEntity` is null, preventing drawing or interaction logic from executing. The drag interaction includes checks to prevent division by zero or collapse to zero scale.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `gl-matrix`
- **Internal:** [EditorService](/services/editor.service.md), [Camera](/omega-game-engine.md), [CanvasViewport](/omega-game-engine.md), [Color](/omega-game-engine.md), [ColorMaterial](/omega-game-engine.md), [Colors](/omega-game-engine.md), [CubePrimitive](/omega-game-engine.md), [DephFunction](/omega-game-engine.md), [SceneEntity](/omega-game-engine.md), [Keybord](/omega-game-engine.md), [MeshData](/omega-game-engine.md), [Mouse](/omega-game-engine.md), [RendererBehaviour](/omega-game-engine.md), [Shader](/omega-game-engine.md), [ShaderSources](/omega-game-engine.md), [ShaderUniformsEnum](/omega-game-engine.md), [Texture](/omega-game-engine.md), [Transform](/omega-game-engine.md), [Vector3](/omega-game-engine.md), [ConeHelper](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/cone.helper.md), [CubeHelper](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/cube.helper.md), [PlaneHelper](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/plane.helper.md), [Raycast](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/raycast.md), [TorusHelper](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/torus.helper.md), [ScaleBoxHelper](/editor/behaviours/scene-editor/scale-box.helper.md)

The `CubeHelper` acts as a concrete implementation detail within the scene editor's rendering pipeline. | Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CubeHelper | Class | Manages the creation, initialization, and rendering of a cube mesh. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The `createMesh` method defines the 8 vertices and the 36 indices required to form the six faces of a cube. The `initialize` method then uploads this raw geometry data to the bound buffers of both the primary shader and the picking shader. The `draw` method handles the rendering loop by binding the correct shader, setting the material color, and executing `gl.drawElements`.

- **Side Effects:** Mutates the internal state of the `Mesh` object by assigning `MeshData`. It interacts directly with the `WebGL2RenderingContext` (`this._gl`) to perform drawing operations.

- **Error Handling:** Checks if `shader?._shaderProgram` exists before attempting to draw, preventing runtime errors if the shader is not properly initialized.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| SoundMixerPlaybackService | editor/components/sound-mixer/sound-mixer.service |

This service is responsible for managing the entire audio playback lifecycle within the editor, from simple single-note previews to complex, timed sequence playback and final WAV file export. It abstracts the low-level audio engine interactions, allowing higher-level components to control playback state (play, pause, stop, seek) based on a defined sequence of musical notes.

It acts as the central controller for audio generation, integrating the `AudioService` to access the underlying `AudioEngine`, `SequencerClock`, and `VoiceFactory`. It translates abstract musical data (`SynthNote[]`) into concrete, time-synced audio events, providing reactive state via Angular signals for UI synchronization.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sequence` | Signal | Exposes the current array of `SynthNote` objects being played. |
| `isPlaying` | Signal | Boolean signal indicating if playback is currently active. |
| `isPaused` | Signal | Boolean signal indicating if playback is paused. |
| `isExporting` | Signal | Boolean signal indicating if the audio export process is running. |
| `playbackTime` | Signal | Current playback time in seconds. |
| `totalDuration` | Computed | Calculates the maximum end time based on the notes in the sequence. |
| `previewPreset` | Method | Triggers a single-note preview using a given `SynthPreset`. |
| `playSequence` | Method | Starts playback of the current sequence, accepting a frame update callback. |
| `pauseSequence` | Method | Pauses the current playback, updating the `playbackTime` based on elapsed time. |
| `stopSequence` | Method | Halts all playback, resets the state, and cleans up active audio nodes. |
| `seekTo` | Method | Jumps playback to a specific time, optionally resuming playback if it was active. |
| `exportWav` | Method | Renders the entire sequence into an offline audio buffer and triggers a WAV file download. |
| `loadDemoSong` | Method | Populates the internal sequence with predefined musical patterns based on a genre type. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** Playback is managed by synchronizing the `SequencerClock` to the BPM derived from the sequence timing. Notes are mapped to specific time steps, and the clock callback triggers the creation and scheduling of audio voices (`triggerNoiseVoice` or `triggerSynthVoice`) at the correct `schedulerTime`. The `animatePlayhead` function uses `requestAnimationFrame` to provide a smooth visual representation of the current time, which is synchronized with the audio clock's progression. Exporting utilizes an `OfflineAudioContext` to render the entire sequence offline before converting the resulting `AudioBuffer` to a WAV Blob.

- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with external state managed by `AudioService` (which manages the `AudioEngine`). It mutates the internal state signals (`sequence`, `isPlaying`, etc.). It triggers browser-level side effects during `exportWav` by creating and clicking a temporary `<a>` element to initiate a file download.

- **Error Handling:** The `previewPreset` and `exportWav` methods use `try...catch` blocks to gracefully handle potential errors during audio node disconnection or rendering failures, ensuring the service state remains stable.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `@angular/core`, `omega-game-engine`
- **Internal:** [AudioService](/editor/services/audio.service.md), [SynthNote](/editor/models/synth.types.md), [SynthPreset](/editor/models/synth.types.md)

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
