| SoundMixerComponent | editor/components/sound-mixer/sound-mixer |

This component serves as the central user interface for the sound design and sequencing module within the editor. Its primary responsibility is to visualize, manipulate, and control musical sequences, allowing users to drag, drop, and edit sound events across multiple tracks. It manages the state for preset selection, timeline navigation, and the interaction between sound definitions and the playback engine.

Architecturally, `SoundMixerComponent` acts as a high-level UI controller that orchestrates interactions between several specialized sub-components and services. It utilizes the [SoundMixerPlaybackService](/editor/components/sound-mixer/sound-mixer.md) to manage playback state, integrates [PresetListComponent](/editor/components/preset-list/preset-list.md) for preset browsing, and provides visual feedback via [OscilloscopeComponent](/editor/components/oscilloscope/oscilloscope.md) and [SoundDesignerComponent](/editor/components/sound-designer/sound-designer.md) when editing specific elements.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `pixelsPerSecond()` | Signal | Getter for the current time resolution in pixels per second. |
| `trackHeight` | Constant | Defines the vertical height allocated for a single audio track. |
| `rulerHeight` | Constant | Defines the vertical height of the timeline ruler area. |
| `trackHeaderWidth` | Constant | Defines the fixed width reserved for track headers. |
| `numTracks` | Constant | The total number of audio tracks available in the mixer. |
| `snapResolution` | Constant | The granularity (in seconds) to which note start times are snapped during drag/drop. |
| `tracks` | Signal | An array representing the available tracks in the mixer. |
| `trackFrequencies` | Readonly Array | An array mapping track indices to default base frequencies (Hz). |
| `presetColors` | Readonly Array | An array of CSS classes used to color-code different preset types. |
| `presets()` | Signal | The current collection of available `SynthPreset` definitions. |
| `isDesignerOpen()` | Signal | Boolean indicating whether the sound designer modal/panel is currently active. |
| `editingPresetId()` | Signal | The ID of the preset currently being edited in the designer. |
| `editingTimelineNoteId()` | Signal | The ID of the timeline note currently being edited in the designer. |
| `designerDraft()` | Signal | The current draft state of the preset or note being edited. |
| `dragIndicator()` | Signal | Holds the calculated position and dimensions of the element being dragged. |
| `timelineWidth()` | Computed | Calculates the total required width of the timeline view based on playback duration and zoom level. |
| `rulerTicks()` | Computed | Generates an array representing the time markers (ticks) for the timeline ruler. |
| `updateZoom(event)` | Method | Updates the `pixelsPerSecond` signal based on user input from a zoom control element. |
| `getDefaultPreset()` | Method | Creates and returns a default, randomized `SynthPreset` object for new creation. |
| `openDesigner(preset?)` | Method | Opens the sound designer, either starting from a provided preset or a new default. |
| `openDesignerForTimelineNote(note)` | Method | Opens the sound designer pre-filled with the properties of an existing `SynthNote`. |
| `closeDesigner()` | Method | Closes the sound designer interface and resets editing states. |
| `savePreset(draft)` | Method | Persists the changes from the designer draft, either updating an existing preset/note or adding a new one. |
| `onDragStartPreset(event, preset)` | Method | Initiates a drag operation for creating a new note from a preset. |
| `onDragStartExistingNote(event, note)` | Method | Initiates a drag operation for moving an existing note. |
| `onDragOver(event)` | Method | Handles the drag-and-drop event to calculate the target position and display the drag indicator. |
| `onDragLeave()` | Method | Clears the drag indicator when the mouse leaves the drop zone. |
| `onDrop(event)` | Method | Finalizes the drag-and-drop operation, creating or moving a note based on the payload. |
| `onRulerClick(event)` | Method | Triggers playback seeking to the time corresponding to the ruler click position. |
| `triggerPlay()` | Method | Starts the playback sequence managed by the service. |
| `removeNote(id)` | Method | Removes a specific note from the playback sequence by its ID. |
| `clearTimeline()` | Method | Clears all notes from the sequence after user confirmation. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component manages complex state transitions related to editing (preset vs. timeline note) using `editingPresetId` and `editingTimelineNoteId`. Drag-and-drop functionality calculates target time and track indices by mapping screen coordinates (`event.clientX`, `event.clientY`) to time/track coordinates using `pixelsPerSecond` and `snapResolution`. When dropping, it either creates a new `SynthNote` based on a preset or updates an existing note's position and track. Playback synchronization is handled by listening to frame updates from the [SoundMixerPlaybackService](/editor/components/sound-mixer/sound-mixer.md) to position the playhead element.

- **Side Effects:** The component interacts heavily with external state: it calls `this.playback.loadDemoSong()` in `ngAfterViewInit` to initialize the sequence, and it calls `this.playback.playSequence()` and `this.playback.seekTo()` to control the audio playback engine. It also mutates the internal `presets` signal and the `playback.sequence` array upon saving or dropping notes.

- **Error Handling:** The `clearTimeline` method uses a standard JavaScript `confirm()` dialog to prevent accidental data loss before clearing the sequence. The drag-and-drop logic includes checks (`if (!this.dragPayload || !this.timelineRef) return;`) to prevent runtime errors if the necessary DOM references are unavailable.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `crypto` (for UUID generation).
- **Internal:** [PresetListComponent](/editor/components/preset-list/preset-list.md), [OscilloscopeComponent](/editor/components/oscilloscope/oscilloscope.md), [SoundDesignerComponent](/editor/components/sound-designer/sound-designer.md), [Icon](/src/app/components/icon/icon.md), [SoundMixerPlaybackService](/editor/components/sound-mixer/sound-mixer.md).

This component is responsible for rendering and managing the hierarchical structure of entities within a game scene, known as the Scene Tree. Its primary responsibility is to translate the raw `Scene` data structure into a navigable, interactive tree view, allowing users to select, manipulate, and inspect entities within the editor environment.

Architecturally, `SceneTree` functions as a critical UI component that acts as a bridge between the core game engine data model (`omega-game-engine`) and the editor's user interface. It subscribes to state changes from `EditorService` and `SceneTreeService` to ensure the displayed tree remains synchronized with the active scene, handling complex operations like entity selection, hierarchy modification (drag-and-drop), and entity instantiation.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `targetScene` | Input | Binds the component to a specific `Scene` instance, triggering tree preparation. |
| `toggleObj` | Method | Toggles the visibility (`show` property) of a given `SceneEntity`. |
| `entitySelected` | Method | Handles click events on entities within the tree, updating selection state and triggering canvas resize. |
| `refreshTree` | Method | Forces a complete recalculation and redraw of the scene tree structure. |
| `handleNodeDropped` | Method | Manages the logic for re-parenting or reordering nodes based on drag-and-drop events. |
| `onNodeDeleted` | Method | Initiates the deletion of an entity and all its descendants from the scene. |
| `onNodeSelected` | Method | Updates the internal selection state when a tree node is clicked, notifying external services. |
| `onSceneTreeAddNewRequested` | Method | Opens the context menu for adding new entities at the current location. |
| `onEntitySelected` | Method | Instantiates and adds a new entity to the scene based on provided metadata. |
| `inspectScene` | Method | Emits the entire scene object through the entity selection service for inspection. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component builds the tree structure by first mapping all scene objects by UUID. It then traverses the scene objects to determine the root entities (those without a grandparent) and recursively builds the `TreeNode` hierarchy using `createNodeListFromObjectArray`. State synchronization is managed via subscriptions to `EditorService` and `SceneTreeService`. Hierarchy manipulation (drag/drop) involves complex traversal (`findNodeAndParent`) and direct mutation of the `children` arrays within the `TreeNode` structure, followed by updating the underlying `SceneEntity` parent transforms.

- **Side Effects:** Mutates the state of the `Scene` object (adding/removing entities, changing entity visibility). Interacts heavily with external services (`EditorService`, `SceneTreeService`) to emit events, which can trigger canvas resizing and scene updates.

- **Error Handling:** Fallbacks are implemented in `findNodeAndParent` to return `{ node: null, parent: null }` if a name is not found. In `onNodeDeleted`, it checks if the entity exists in `treeNodeMap` before attempting deletion.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `CommonModule`, `Icon`
- **Internal:** [SceneTreeService](/editor/components/scene-tree/scene-tree.md), [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md), [SceneEntity](/omega-game-engine/scene-entity.md), [EntityType](/omega-game-engine/entity-type.md), [Scene](/omega-game-engine/scene.md), [ObjectInstanciator](/omega-game-engine/object-instanciator.md), [ClassMetadata](/omega-game-engine/class-metadata.md), [ClassType](/omega-game-engine/class-type.md)

## 1. Overview & Purpose

This component is responsible for rendering a collapsible panel, typically used within an editor interface to display inspector details. Its primary function is to manage the visibility state of its content, allowing users to expand or collapse the panel via a toggle mechanism. It accepts various configuration inputs to customize its appearance and behavior.

Architecturally, `InpectorTogglePanel` serves as a presentation layer UI component. It consumes configuration data via `@Input()` properties (such as `title`, `collapsed`, and `isChild`) and communicates state changes externally by emitting a `toggle` event via `@Output()`. It relies on the `Icon` component for visual representation.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| title | Input | The display title for the panel. Defaults to 'NoName'. |
| collapsed | Input | The current collapsed state of the panel. Defaults to false. |
| isAbleToCollapse | Input | Determines if the panel can be collapsed. Defaults to true. |
| isChild | Input | Indicates if this panel is a child element within a larger structure. Defaults to false. |
| rightAlign | Input | Controls the alignment of the panel elements on the right side. Defaults to false. |
| toggle | Output | Emits a boolean value representing the new collapsed state when the toggle action is performed. |
| onToggle | Method | Handles the internal logic for toggling the collapsed state and emitting the event. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The `onToggle` method inverts the current `collapsed` state, updates the component's internal state, and then emits the new state via the `toggle` EventEmitter.
- **Side Effects:** None. The component manages its state internally and communicates changes via events, without direct external I/O.
- **Error Handling:** None.

This component is responsible for rendering and managing the visibility and interaction of a context menu displayed over a specific file node within the editor interface. It encapsulates the logic for showing the menu at a precise screen coordinate and handling user interactions like clicking on menu items or clicking outside the menu area to dismiss it.

Architecturally, this component functions as a presentation layer UI component. It consumes its state via a `model` input, which dictates its visibility and content, and emits an event (`actionExecuted`) when a user selects an action, allowing parent components to handle the resulting business logic against the associated [FileNode](/editor/components/file-explorer/file-explorer.model.md).

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ContextMenuState | Interface | Defines the structure for the menu's state, including visibility, position (x, y), the associated file node, and available actions. |
| actionExecuted | EventEmitter | Emits an event containing the selected `ContextMenuAction` and the associated `FileNode` when a menu item is clicked. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component manages its visibility using a reactive `model` input. It listens globally to `document:click` events to implement a "click-outside" dismissal mechanism. When an action is clicked, it stops propagation, emits the execution event, and then closes the menu.
- **Side Effects:** Mutates the internal state (`this.state`) to control visibility. It interacts with the global DOM via `HostListener` to capture document-level events.
- **Error Handling:** No explicit error handling is implemented; dismissal relies on the `document:click` listener checking if the click target is within the component's element.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**

- **Internal:** [CommonModule](/common/common.module.md)

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| Canvas | /editor/components/canvas/canvas.md |

This component is responsible for hosting and managing the primary rendering surface for the editor's 3D scene, utilizing a WebGL2 context. Its primary responsibility is to orchestrate the game engine's lifecyclehandling updates, rendering frames, and managing performance statisticswithin the browser's animation loop. It acts as the bridge between the high-level editor state and the low-level graphics API.

Architecturally, `Canvas` functions as a core UI component that integrates deeply with the application's state management via services like [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md) and [EditorSettingsService](/editor/services/editor.settings.md). It subscribes to global events (like resize or reset) to maintain synchronization with the editor's overall state, ensuring the rendering context is always correctly configured and active.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| onGlContextCreated | EventEmitter | Emitted when the WebGL2 context has been successfully initialized. |
| stats | EventEmitter | Emitted periodically containing performance metrics (FPS, frame times). |
| gizmoMode | GizmoMode | Current mode for gizmo interactions (e.g., Translate, Rotate). |
| transformSpace | TransformSpace | Current coordinate space used for transformations (e.g., Local, World). |
| setGizmoMode | Method | Sets the gizmo mode by calling the corresponding method on [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md). |
| toggleTransformSpace | Method | Switches the current transformation space between World and Local. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component runs a continuous animation loop driven by `requestAnimationFrame`. In each frame, it first checks if rendering is permitted via `shouldRender()`. If permitted, it calculates the delta time, executes the engine's `update()` method, and then conditionally executes the `executeRenderPass()` if enough time has passed since the last draw cycle (based on `frameInterval`). Performance metrics are tracked and emitted every second.
- **Side Effects:** The component heavily mutates external state by interacting with the WebGL context (`this.gl`) and the `EditorService`. It also subscribes to global events from `EditorService` and uses `requestAnimationFrame` to drive the rendering loop.
- **Error Handling:** It includes `try...catch` blocks around engine initialization and update/render calls to prevent application crashes due to user code errors within the engine.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `rxjs`, `performance` (Browser API)
- **Internal:** [EditorService](/editor/services/editor.service.md), [EditorSettingsService](/editor/services/editor.settings.md), [Icon](/src/app/components/icon/icon.md)

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| OmegaLoggerPanelComponent | editor/components/problems-panel/problems-panel |

This component is responsible for displaying and managing a real-time log panel within the editor interface. It subscribes to logs generated by the application's logging system, allowing users to view, filter, and interact with diagnostic messages. Its primary function is to provide a persistent, updatable view of system events.

Architecturally, this component functions as a dedicated UI component responsible for presentation logic. It interacts heavily with the global state managed by [EngineLogger](/src/engine/logger.md) to pull log data, and utilizes Angular's change detection mechanism via [ChangeDetectorRef](/@angular/core.md) to ensure the view updates efficiently when new logs arrive.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `logs` | LogEntry[] | The array holding all currently loaded log entries. |
| `selectedLevel` | string | Controls the filtering of displayed logs (e.g., "all", "error"). |

| `getLogSummary` | Method | Extracts the main message from a log entry, stripping away the stack trace. |
| `getStackTrace` | Method | Extracts only the stack trace portion from a log entry. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component initializes by fetching the current logs and sets up a recurring interval timer to poll the `EngineLogger` every 250ms. - **Side Effects:** Mutates external/global state by calling `EngineLogger.getLogs()` and `EngineLogger.clear()`. It uses `setInterval` to actively poll the logger service.
- **Error Handling:** No explicit try/catch blocks are present; state changes rely on the synchronous nature of the logger retrieval.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| AssetsExplorerService | [editor/components/asset-explorer/assets-explorer.service](/editor/components/asset-explorer/assets-explorer.service.md) |

This service is responsible for managing the entire asset browsing experience within the editor. Its primary responsibility is to fetch, structure, and maintain the state of all project assets, presenting them in a navigable tree structure that users can interact with. It handles the logic for creating, renaming, and deleting assets based on user actions.

Architecturally, this service acts as a centralized state manager and API client for asset operations. It consumes data from the [AssetService](/app/api/services/asset.service.md) and interacts with the [EditorStateService](/editor/components/asset-explorer/editor-state.service.md) to synchronize selections and folder activations across the application.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| loadProjectAssets | Method | Fetches all assets for a given project ID and builds the internal asset tree structure. |
| selectNode | Method | Handles user selection on an asset node, either toggling expansion for folders or setting the selected asset for files. |
| activateFolder | Method | Sets a specific folder or project as the currently active context for asset operations. |
| toggleExpand | Method | Toggles the expanded/collapsed state of a given asset node. |
| createAsset | Method | Creates a new asset (file or folder) based on a specified action type and name, uploading it via the API. |
| renameAsset | Method | Updates the virtual path (name) of an existing asset within the project. |
| deleteAsset | Method | Removes an asset from the project, updating the local state upon successful deletion. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service maintains state using Angular Signals (`treeData`, `selectedNodeId`, `expandedNodes`, `activeFolder`). Asset tree construction (`buildAssetTree`) recursively maps flat asset responses into a hierarchical structure based on `virtualPath`. Asset creation (`createAsset`) uses a switch statement to determine file content, MIME type, and extension based on the requested action type.
- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with the network via `AssetService` methods (`listAssets`, `uploadAsset`, `updateAsset`, `deleteAsset`). It also mutates the external state managed by `EditorStateService`.
- **Error Handling:** `createAsset` returns `null` if the action type is unknown or if the action is 'folder' (which requires backend support). `deleteAsset` handles state cleanup if the deleted node was the active folder or the currently selected asset.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `rxjs`
- **Internal:** [AssetService](/app/api/services/asset.service.md), [EditorStateService](/editor/components/asset-explorer/editor-state.service.md)

## 1. Overview & Purpose

| FileSystemService | [file-system.service](/editor/components/file-explorer/file-system.service.md) |

This service is responsible for managing the state and retrieval of file system data within the editor application. It simulates interaction with a complex, hierarchical file structure by using a hardcoded `MOCK_FILE_SYSTEM` object. Its primary responsibility is to provide observable streams of directory contents and methods to fetch the content of specific files based on their paths.

Architecturally, `FileSystemService` acts as a dedicated data access layer or service layer. It abstracts the complexity of traversing the mock file system, allowing UI components to subscribe to changes in the current directory state via `currentDirectory$` or request specific file contents using `getFileContent`. It relies on the `FileNode` model for its data structure.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `currentDirectory$` | Observable | An observable stream that emits an array of `FileNode` objects representing the contents of the currently viewed directory. |
| `navigateToDirectory(path: string)` | Method | Initiates a navigation sequence to a specified path, updating the `currentDirectory$` stream after a simulated delay. |
| `getFileContent(path: string)` | Method | Returns an observable that emits the simulated content string for a file located at the given path. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service maintains state using a `BehaviorSubject` to track the current directory's contents. Navigation is handled by recursively searching the `MOCK_FILE_SYSTEM` using `findNodeByPath`. When navigating, it simulates asynchronous behavior using RxJS `delay` operators to mimic network latency before emitting the children of the target directory. File content retrieval also simulates an asynchronous read operation.

- **Side Effects:** The code simulates network latency and asynchronous file reading/navigation via RxJS `delay` operators, which mimics external I/O operations. It mutates the internal state managed by `currentDirectorySubject`.

- **Error Handling:** If `navigateToDirectory` is called with a path that does not exist or is not a directory, the service falls back to emitting the children of the root directory (`MOCK_FILE_SYSTEM.children`). `getFileContent` returns a specific error string if the path does not resolve to a file.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** RxJS
- **Internal:** [file-explorer.model](/editor/components/file-explorer/file-explorer.model.md)

It consumes time-domain audio data from the AudioService's AnalyserNode to draw a dynamic line graph representing the signal's amplitude over time. It manages its lifecycle by setting up and tearing down the requestAnimationFrame loop and handling canvas resizing events.
nodes.human_overview:
This component is responsible for visualizing the real-time audio waveform data captured from the application's audio engine. It utilizes the HTML Canvas API to draw a dynamic representation of the time-domain audio signal, allowing users to visually inspect the frequency and amplitude characteristics of the sound being processed.

Architecturally, this component functions as a specialized UI visualization layer. It relies heavily on the `AudioService` to access the underlying `AnalyserNode` from the core audio engine, positioning it as a consumer of low-level audio processing data to render a user-facing diagnostic tool.
nodes.side_effects: Interacts with the global `window` object to listen for `resize` events and uses `requestAnimationFrame` to drive continuous rendering. It mutates the canvas element's drawing context.
nodes.raw_markdown:
## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| OscilloscopeComponent | [oscilloscope](/editor/components/sound-mixer/components/oscilloscope/oscilloscope.component.md) |

This component is responsible for visualizing the real-time audio waveform data captured from the application's audio engine. It utilizes the HTML Canvas API to draw a dynamic representation of the time-domain audio signal, allowing users to visually inspect the frequency and amplitude characteristics of the sound being processed.

Architecturally, this component functions as a specialized UI visualization layer. It relies heavily on the `AudioService` to access the underlying `AnalyserNode` from the core audio engine, positioning it as a consumer of low-level audio processing data to render a user-facing diagnostic tool.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
This file contains no public exports.

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component initializes an `AnalyserNode` via the `AudioService` upon view initialization. It then sets up a continuous animation loop using `requestAnimationFrame`. In each frame, it retrieves the time-domain data from the analyser, clears the canvas, and draws a line graph connecting points sampled from the `Uint8Array` data, scaled to fit the canvas dimensions.
- **Side Effects:** Interacts with the global `window` object to listen for `resize` events and uses `requestAnimationFrame` to drive continuous rendering. It mutates the canvas element's drawing context.
- **Error Handling:** It includes checks to ensure `this.analyser` and `this.canvasRef` are available before starting the drawing loop. It also checks if the canvas context (`ctx`) can be successfully retrieved.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** None
- **Internal:** [AudioService](/editor/services/audio.service.md)

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| TreeNodeComponent | editor/components/scene-tree/tree-node/tree-node.md |

This component is responsible for rendering a single node within the scene tree visualization. Its primary function is to display the node's data, handle user interactions such as selection, deletion, and drag-and-drop operations, and manage the visual state related to potential drop zones (above, below, inside).

Architecturally, `TreeNodeComponent` acts as a presentation layer UI component. It consumes node data via the `@Input()` property `node` and communicates user actionslike selection changes or structural modificationsupwards to its parent components via `@Output()` events, such as `nodeSelected` or `nodeDropped`. It relies on `TreeNode` for its data structure and `Icon` for visual representation.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `nodeDropped` | EventEmitter | Emitted when a node is successfully dropped onto this node, providing the dragged node, target node, and drop position. |
| `visibilityChange` | EventEmitter | Emitted when the visibility state of the node changes. |
| `nodeSelected` | EventEmitter | Emitted when the node is clicked and selected, provided the selected node object. |
| `nodeDeleted` | EventEmitter | Emitted when the node is deleted, providing the deleted node object. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component implements complex drag-and-drop logic. `onDragOver` calculates the vertical position of the mouse relative to the node's bounding box to determine if the drop intent is 'above', 'below', or 'inside'. `onDrop` then parses the JSON data of the dragged node and emits the `nodeDropped` event with the determined drop position. Selection is managed by comparing the clicked node's ID against the `selectedNodeId` input.

- **Side Effects:** The component emits events (`nodeDropped`, `nodeSelected`, `nodeDeleted`) which trigger state changes in parent components, effectively mutating the application's global state (the scene tree structure). It also uses `console.debug` for logging.

- **Error Handling:** The `onDrop` method includes a check to ensure the `draggedNode` exists and that it is not the same as the `this.node` to prevent self-dropping errors.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `DragEvent`, `MouseEvent` (Browser APIs)
- **Internal:** [Icon](/editor/components/icon/icon.md), [TreeNode](/editor/components/scene-tree/tree-node/tree-node.md)

nodes.name: OmegaDropzoneComponent
nodes.semantic_summary: OmegaDropzoneComponent implements a reusable, interactive UI dropzone for asset uploads within the asset explorer. It manages file ingestion via two mechanisms: native drag-and-drop events and a triggered file input dialog. Architecturally, it encapsulates complex DOM event handling, using Angular Signals to manage visual states (isDragging) and emits collected File objects through the filesDropped output for downstream processing.
nodes.human_overview:

Its primary responsibility is to manage the visual state of the dropzoneindicating when files are being dragged over itand to emit the collected `File` objects to consuming parts of the application.

Architecturally, this component functions as a specialized UI component within the asset explorer module. It encapsulates the complex DOM event handling required for drag-and-drop operations (`dragover`, `dragleave`, `drop`) and file input selection. It communicates its results externally via the `filesDropped` output, allowing parent components to handle the subsequent asset processing or storage logic.
nodes.side_effects: Interacts with the browser's DOM and file system access layer (via the native `File` object). It triggers the native file input element's click event.

This component provides a reusable, interactive dropzone interface designed to accept file uploads from the user via drag-and-drop or by triggering a native file picker dialog. Its primary responsibility is to manage the visual state of the dropzoneindicating when files are being dragged over itand to emit the collected `File` objects to consuming parts of the application.

Architecturally, this component functions as a specialized UI component within the asset explorer module. It encapsulates the complex DOM event handling required for drag-and-drop operations (`dragover`, `dragleave`, `drop`) and file input selection. It communicates its results externally via the `filesDropped` output, allowing parent components to handle the subsequent asset processing or storage logic.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| filesDropped | Output | Emits an array of `File` objects when files are successfully dropped or selected. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component manages two primary input mechanisms: a native `<input type="file">` triggered by a click, and native browser drag-and-drop events. It uses Angular Signals (`isDragging`) to manage the visual state, which is bound to the host element's class. When a drop occurs, it prevents default browser behavior, extracts the `FileList`, and emits the files.
- **Side Effects:** Interacts with the browser's DOM and file system access layer (via the native `File` object). It triggers the native file input element's click event.
- **Error Handling:** The component handles the absence of files during drop or selection by checking `event.dataTransfer?.files` or `input.files` before emitting, preventing runtime errors from empty lists.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** None
- **Internal:** None

It utilizes a signal-based queue to stage files dropped via OmegaDropzoneComponent, allowing users to configure metadata like custom names and asset types. Its primary role is to collect, validate, and emit the final array of StagedAssetResult upon user confirmation, while providing clear cancellation pathways.

It manages the staging process, allowing users to drag-and-drop files or browse for them, while simultaneously allowing them to configure metadata for each file, such as a custom filename and asset type. Its primary responsibility is to collect and validate these staged items before committing them to the editor's asset pipeline.

It utilizes signals (`queue`) to manage the transient state of staged items and exposes public outputs (`confirmed`, `closed`) to communicate the final batch of assets or the cancellation event back to its parent controller. It relies on the `OmegaDropzoneComponent` for file ingestion and handles the internal logic for inferring asset types based on file extensions.
nodes.side_effects: None. The component manages internal state via signals and emits events; it does not directly interact with the network or filesystem.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| OmegaUploadModalComponent | [omega-upload-modal](/editor/components/asset-explorer/components/omega-upload-modal.component.ts.md) |

This component is responsible for providing a user interface for batch importing assets into the editor environment. It manages the staging process, allowing users to drag-and-drop files or browse for them, while simultaneously allowing them to configure metadata for each file, such as a custom filename and asset type. Its primary responsibility is to collect and validate these staged items before committing them to the editor's asset pipeline.

Architecturally, this component functions as a dedicated UI modal layer. It utilizes signals (`queue`) to manage the transient state of staged items and exposes public outputs (`confirmed`, `closed`) to communicate the final batch of assets or the cancellation event back to its parent controller. It relies on the `OmegaDropzoneComponent` for file ingestion and handles the internal logic for inferring asset types based on file extensions.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `targetFolderColumn` | Input | Provides the target directory path where assets will be imported. |
| `confirmed` | Output | Emitted when the user confirms the batch import, containing an array of `StagedAssetResult`. |
| `closed` | Output | Emitted when the user cancels the modal operation. |
| `queue` | Signal | A read-only signal holding the current array of `LocalStagedItem` objects awaiting confirmation. |
| `onFilesIngested` | Method | Processes an array of dropped `File` objects, adding them to the staging queue with inferred metadata. |
| `removeRow` | Method | Removes a specific staged item from the queue using its unique ID. |
| `onCancel` | Method | Triggers the `closed` output event, dismissing the modal. |
| `onConfirm` | Method | Triggers the `confirmed` output event, passing the current staged items as `StagedAssetResult[]`. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component maintains a queue of staged assets. When files are ingested, they are added to this queue, and metadata (like size formatting and initial asset type inference) is calculated. The user can then modify the `customName` and `assetType` for each item within the queue. Upon confirmation, the component maps the internal `LocalStagedItem` structure to the external `StagedAssetResult` structure and emits it.
- **Side Effects:** None. The component manages internal state via signals and emits events; it does not directly interact with the network or filesystem.
- **Error Handling:** The component relies on the `inferAssetType` method to provide a default ('raw') if an extension cannot be matched, ensuring the queue always contains a valid asset type.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `FormsModule`
- **Internal:** [OmegaDropzoneComponent](/editor/components/asset-explorer/components/omega-dropzone.component.ts.md)

It acts as a presentation layer, consuming engine state to expose a 'create' output emitter for triggering asset creation actions.
nodes.human_overview:
This component is responsible for dynamically generating a menu structure that lists all available asset types within the project. It achieves this by introspecting the metadata provided by the `ObjectInstanciator` to discover all registered types, filtering out internal or unwanted types, and organizing the discovered assets into a hierarchical, tree-like structure suitable for display in a user interface.

Architecturally, this component acts as a presentation layer component that consumes metadata from the `ObjectInstanciator` and utilizes the `AssetsExplorerService` for potential asset-related operations. It transforms raw metadata into a structured `IAsset` tree, which is then exposed via the `create` output emitter to trigger asset creation actions elsewhere in the application.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| AssetCreateMenuComponent | [asset-create-menu](/editor/components/asset-explorer/components/asset-create-menu/asset-create-menu.md) |

This component is responsible for dynamically generating a menu structure that lists all available asset types within the project. It achieves this by introspecting the metadata provided by the `ObjectInstanciator` to discover all registered types, filtering out internal or unwanted types, and organizing the discovered assets into a hierarchical, tree-like structure suitable for display in a user interface.

Architecturally, this component acts as a presentation layer component that consumes metadata from the `ObjectInstanciator` and utilizes the `AssetsExplorerService` for potential asset-related operations. It transforms raw metadata into a structured `IAsset` tree, which is then exposed via the `create` output emitter to trigger asset creation actions elsewhere in the application.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| IMenuAction | Interface | Defines the structure for a menu item, including label, optional icon, action string, and nested children. |
| IAsset | Interface | Defines the structure for an asset node in the generated tree, including ID, name, type, and children. |
| AssetCreateMenuComponent | Class | The main component class responsible for building and managing the asset creation menu data. |
| create | Output | An output emitter that emits a string representing the action to be performed when a menu item is selected. |
| handleAction | Method | Handles mouse events on menu items, stopping propagation and emitting the associated action if provided. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component initializes by filtering all available object metadata from `ObjectInstanciator.getMetadata()` to exclude specific types. It then groups these items by their path into a map. The core logic resides in `buildAssetTree`, which recursively constructs a tree structure. It uses an `ensureFolder` helper to guarantee the existence of parent folders for every item's path, ensuring a complete hierarchy before populating the nodes. Finally, it performs a depth-first sort on the resulting tree to prioritize folders over files and maintain alphabetical order within groups.

- **Side Effects:** The component reads metadata from `ObjectInstanciator.getMetadata()`, which constitutes reading internal engine state. It also logs data to the console during initialization.

- **Error Handling:** The `ensureFolder` helper uses recursion and a `Map` (`nodeMap`) to prevent infinite loops and ensure that folder creation is idempotent, effectively handling path construction errors by relying on the map lookup.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** None.
- **Internal:** [AssetsExplorerService](/editor/components/asset-explorer/assets-explorer.service.md)

The `startLabelDrag` method initiates a global mouse listener setup to track movement (`handleLabelMove`). During dragging, the change in X position is translated into a proportional change in the range value based on a fixed pixel-to-range mapping (`pixelsForFullRange`). | OmegaEngineService | app/services/omega-engine.service.md |

This service is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the game engine instance within the application. Its primary responsibility is to dynamically load, initialize, and manage the execution of game modules fetched from a remote backend endpoint. It handles the complex process of fetching a bundled game module based on a provided project ID and instantiating the `Engine` class from that module.

Architecturally, this component functions as a core service layer responsible for runtime dependency injection and dynamic module loading. It acts as the bridge between the application's core logic and the external, dynamically loaded game code. It relies on configuration from [api-url](/app/api/api-url.md) and communicates state changes via its public `EventEmitter`s, such as [reloadEngineRequested](/app/services/omega-engine.service.md).

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| isReloadingEngine | Getter | Returns a boolean indicating if an engine reload process is currently active. |
| currentEngine | Getter | Returns the currently active `Engine` instance, or `null` if none is loaded. |
| reloadEngineRequested | EventEmitter | Emits an event signal when a reload of the engine is requested. |
| engineReloaded | EventEmitter | Emits an event with a boolean indicating the success or failure of the last engine reload attempt. |
| onReloadEngine | Method | Initiates the asynchronous process to fetch and load a new engine instance for a specified project ID. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The `onReloadEngine` method first emits a request signal and sets an internal reloading flag. It constructs a dynamic URL to fetch a bundled JavaScript module containing the game logic. It then uses dynamic `import()` to load this module. Upon successful loading, it checks for the exported `Game` class, destroys any existing engine instance, instantiates the new engine, and registers its dependencies before emitting a success event.
- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with the network via dynamic `import()` calls to fetch remote bundles. It also reads from `localStorage` to retrieve the authentication token and mutates internal state (`_isReloadingEngine`, `_currentEngine`).
- **Error Handling:** It employs a comprehensive `try...catch` block to handle network failures or module loading errors. Specific checks are in place to validate the presence of a `projectId` and an authentication token. If loading fails at any stage, it logs a critical error, emits `engineReloaded(false)`, and resets the reloading state.

**Environment & Configuration:**

| confirmationRequest$ | Observable | An observable stream exposing all confirmation requests that have been initiated. |
| confirm | Method | Initiates a new confirmation prompt. It takes a `ConfirmationRequest` and returns an `Observable<boolean>` that resolves when the user responds. |
| respond | Method | Informs the service of the user's choice (true for confirm, false for cancel), completing the active confirmation observable stream. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service uses two RxJS Subjects: `confirmationRequestSubject` to broadcast all requests, and `currentResultSubject` to manage the state of the *currently active* prompt. When `confirm` is called, it sets up a new `currentResultSubject` and pushes the request. When `respond` is called, it pushes the result to that specific subject and completes it, effectively resolving the promise/observable returned by `confirm`.

- **Side Effects:** None. The service manages internal state via RxJS Subjects but does not interact with the network, filesystem, or external global state.

- **Error Handling:** The service relies on the completion of the `currentResultSubject` to signal the end of a prompt. If `respond` is called when no active subject exists, the call is silently ignored.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

- **Internal:** None

This component serves as the primary bridge between the Angular application environment and the external .NET WebAssembly runtime. Its core responsibility is managing the lifecycle of the .NET runtime, ensuring it is initialized correctly, and providing typed access to the exported functionalities from the `omega-engine-core.dll` assembly.

Architecturally, this service acts as a critical integration layer within the application's service layer. It abstracts the complex asynchronous loading and configuration of the WebAssembly runtime, allowing other parts of the application to interact with engine logic (like `EngineMath`) through a clean, promise-based interface, such as the `calculateTransform` method.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| OmegaEngineExports | Interface | Defines the expected structure of the exports object returned by the .NET runtime, including nested structures like `OmegaCore` and `EngineMath`. |
| OmegaCoreBridgeService | Class | Manages the connection and interaction with the .NET WebAssembly runtime. |
| initializeEngine | Method | Asynchronously initializes the .NET runtime, loading necessary assemblies and returning the full exports object. |
| runTestCalculation | Method | Executes a predefined test calculation using the initialized engine exports and logs the result. |
| calculateTransform | Method | Public method to execute the `CalculateTransform` function from the engine, requiring initialization first. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service first checks its internal state (`isInitialized`). If not initialized, it dynamically imports the `dotnet.js` script. It then configures the .NET runtime with specific assembly names and resource loaders. It attempts to retrieve assembly exports from `omega-engine-core.dll`, falling back to `omega-engine-core` if the first attempt fails. Subsequent calls use the cached `dotNetExports`.
- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with the network by dynamically importing external JavaScript modules (`/assets/wasm/dotnet.js`) and loading WebAssembly binaries/DLLs from the `/assets/wasm/` directory. It mutates internal state (`dotNetExports`, `isInitialized`).
- **Error Handling:** It uses `try...catch` blocks extensively. Initialization errors are caught, logged, and re-thrown. A specific fallback mechanism is implemented when retrieving assembly exports, attempting to load without the `.dll` extension if the initial attempt fails.

- **Internal:** None

## 1. Overview & Purpose

| :--- | :--- |
| AuthInterceptor | app/api/auth.interceptor |

This interceptor is responsible for automatically injecting the user's authentication token into every outgoing HTTP request made by the application. Its primary function is to ensure that API calls are properly authenticated by attaching the token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, thereby securing communication with backend services.

Architecturally, this component acts as a crucial middleware layer within the Angular HTTP client pipeline. It sits between the application services and the network layer, leveraging the `AuthService` to retrieve credentials and the `Router` to manage application flow upon authentication failure.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| AuthInterceptor | Class | Implements `HttpInterceptor`. Intercepts requests to add authorization headers and handles 401 errors by redirecting to the login page. |
| intercept | Method | Processes an outgoing HTTP request. It clones the request to inject the token and pipes the result through error handling logic. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The interceptor checks for an existing token via `authService.getToken()`. If found, it clones the incoming `HttpRequest` and sets the `Authorization` header. It then handles the response stream, specifically catching `HttpErrorResponse` with status 401. If a 401 is detected, it clears the local session via `authService.clearLocalSession()` and navigates the user to `/login` using `router.navigate(['/login'])`.

- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with the network (by intercepting HTTP requests), mutates external state (by calling `authService.clearLocalSession()`), and modifies the application state by triggering navigation via `router.navigate()`.

- **Error Handling:** It explicitly catches `HttpErrorResponse`. If the status is 401, it performs a session clear and redirection. In all other error cases, it passes the original error downstream using `throwError(() => error)`.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `@angular/common/http`, `@angular/core`, `@angular/router`
- **Internal:** [AuthService](/app/api/services/auth.service.md)

This component provides a comprehensive, interactive color selection interface, allowing users to pick colors using a visual color area, a hue slider, and an alpha slider. Its primary responsibility is to translate user interactions (mouse movements, slider drags) into precise color values across multiple color models (RGB, HSV, HSL, CMYK) and emit these changes to the parent component.

Architecturally, `ColorPickerComponent` functions as a specialized UI component responsible for state management of color properties (`hue`, `saturation`, `value`, `alpha`). It utilizes Angular's lifecycle hooks and `NgZone` to manage DOM events and coordinate updates across its internal state and external output via the `colorChange` EventEmitter, fitting squarely into the application's presentation layer.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| color | Input | Binds an initial color object `{ r: number, g: number, b: number, a: number }` to initialize the picker state. |
| colorChange | Output | Emits an event containing the current color in both RGBA and Hex formats upon any change. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The component maintains state using HSV, which is derived from the input RGB values. User interaction updates `saturation` (via color area X), `value` (via color area Y), `hue` (via hue slider X), and `alpha` (via alpha slider Y). All changes trigger `updateAllColors()`, which recalculates the corresponding RGB, Hex, CMYK, and HSL values. Its primary responsibility is to fetch scene assets from the backend API when a project context is provided and to manage the user interface for scene selection and creation.

Architecturally, `SceneList` functions as a presentation and controller component within the UI layer. It relies heavily on the `AssetService` for all data interactions (listing and uploading assets) and uses the `Router` to navigate the user to the editor view upon scene selection. It consumes the `ProjectResponse` input to scope its operations.

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `project` | Input | The `ProjectResponse` object containing project metadata, used to scope asset loading and creation. |
| `scenes` | Property | An array holding the `AssetResponse` objects representing the scenes available in the current project. |
| `isModalOpen` | Property | Boolean state controlling the visibility of the "Create New Scene" modal. |
| `newSceneName` | Property | String holding the name input for a newly created scene. |
| `navigateToEditor(scene: AssetResponse)` | Method | Navigates the user to the editor view for the specified scene ID within the current project. |
| `openNewSceneModal()` | Method | Triggers the display of the modal interface for creating a new scene. |
| `closeModal()` | Method | Hides the creation modal and resets the input field. |
| `createScene()` | Method | Handles the logic for creating a new scene by generating a file object and uploading it via the `AssetService`. |

- **Side Effects:** The code interacts heavily with the network via `AssetService.listAssets` and `AssetService.uploadAsset`. It also mutates the component's internal state (`scenes`, `isModalOpen`, `newSceneName`) and uses the `Router` to navigate the application.

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** Upon initialization (`ngOnInit`), the component checks the authentication status. - **Error Handling:** If `userService.getMe()` fails (e.g., due to an expired or invalid token), the component catches the error and automatically calls `authService.logout()` to invalidate the session.

## 1. Overview & Purpose
| Component | Source File |
| :--- | :--- |
| AuthService | app/api/services/auth.service |

This service is responsible for encapsulating all business logic related to user authentication within the application. Its primary responsibility is to manage the lifecycle of user sessions, including registration, secure login, and logout operations by communicating with the backend API. It handles the persistence of the authentication token locally to maintain the user's logged-in state across sessions.

Architecturally, `AuthService` functions as a dedicated service layer component. It acts as the intermediary between the application's business logic and the external authentication endpoints, utilizing the `HttpClient` to make network requests. It relies on models defined in [omega-api.models](/src/app/models/omega-api.models.md) and interacts with the application's token configuration via [API_URL](/src/api-url.token.md).

## 2. Public API & Interfaces
| Entity | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| register | Method | Registers a new user by sending registration data to the API. Returns an Observable of `UserResponse`. |
| login | Method | Authenticates an existing user. Upon success, it stores the returned `accessToken` in `localStorage`. Returns an Observable of `LoginResponse`. |
| logout | Method | Initiates the logout process by calling the API and subsequently clearing the local session token. Returns an Observable of `MessageResponse`. |
| getToken | Method | Retrieves the stored authentication token from `localStorage`. Returns the token string or `null`. |
| isLoggedIn | Method | Checks the current authentication status by verifying the presence of a token in `localStorage`. Returns a boolean. |
| clearLocalSession | Method | Removes the authentication token from `localStorage`, effectively logging the user out client-side. |

## 3. Implementation Details & Side Effects
- **Core Logic:** The service uses RxJS `tap` operators to execute side effects (like token storage or session clearing) immediately after a successful HTTP response is received. Token retrieval and session management rely on checking the existence of `localStorage` to ensure compatibility across different environments.
- **Side Effects:** Interacts heavily with the network via `HttpClient` for all API calls. It also mutates global state by reading from and writing to `localStorage` to persist the authentication token.
- **Error Handling:** The service relies on the underlying `HttpClient` and RxJS stream error handling. Specific API errors (like 401 Unauthorized) are expected to be handled by an external `AuthInterceptor`, which triggers the `clearLocalSession` mechanism.

## 4. Dependencies & Configuration
**Environment & Configuration:**
- No environment variables or external configurations required.

**Module Dependencies:**
- **Standard/External:** `HttpClient`, `Observable`, `tap` (from RxJS).
- **Internal:** [omega-api.models](/src/app/models/omega-api.models.md), [API_URL](/src/api-url.token.md).
